precepts.text: The virgin, the daughter of Zion, hath despised thee and laughed thee to scorn. The angel of the Lord smote a hundred and eighty-five thousand Assyrians overnight, and Sennacherib returned to Nineveh, where his own sons killed him with the sword while he worshipped his god. You will not one-up God; he will one-up you, and that includes the online mockers of God's prophets.
precepts.point: Sennacherib king of Assyria took Judah's defenced cities and sent Rabshakeh to mock Hezekiah in the Jews' language, boasting that no god of any nation had delivered his land out of the king of Assyria's hand.

note.label: The Pride Of Thine Heart

precepts.why:
Pride destroyed every kingdom on the earth, and Assyria is the first king in line. Sennacherib took all the defenced cities of Judah, then sent Rabshakeh, his herald, with big words: “What confidence is this wherein thou trustest?” When Hezekiah's men begged him to speak in the Syrian language so the people on the wall would not hear, he said he was sent to “the men that sit upon the wall, that they may eat their own dung, and drink their own piss with you.” Then he mocked the Lord himself: “Hath any of the gods of the nations delivered his land out of the hand of the king of Assyria?” … “that the Lord should deliver Jerusalem out of my hand?” All that pride came out of the king of Assyria's mouth by way of his messenger.

God heard all that smack. “Thus saith the Lord God of Israel, Whereas thou hast prayed to me against Sennacherib king of Assyria: This is the word which the Lord hath spoken concerning him; The virgin, the daughter of Zion, hath despised thee, and laughed thee to scorn; the daughter of Jerusalem hath shaken her head at thee.” She is laughing at this man's tough talk, the way a parent shakes their head when they told you not to do it and are about to whoop your ass. You are not going to one-up God, and that goes for everyone making videos mocking God's prophets. God will one-up you.

“For I will defend this city to save it for mine own sake, and for my servant David’s sake. Then the angel of the Lord went forth, and smote in the camp of the Assyrians a hundred and fourscore and five thousand.” One of God's angels destroyed 185,000. The sun went down and they were all alive; at the crack of the morning, “they were all dead corpses.” Talking prideful against God, everybody had to die.

But God was hunting Sennacherib himself. “So Sennacherib king of Assyria departed, and went and returned, and dwelt at Nineveh.” He thought he got away. Then “as he was worshipping in the house of Nisroch his god”, his own sons “smote him with the sword”, and they escaped into Armenia, and his other son Esarhaddon reigned in his stead and didn't even care.

Pride destroyed the king of Assyria, as “a man’s pride shall bring him low” in Proverbs 29. And it is the same line through every kingdom after him, Babylon, the Greeks, Rome and America: none is exempt from pride, and none is exempt from God destroying them for it.

precepts.text: Tobit walked in truth and justice and did many alms deeds to his brethren in captivity.
precepts.point: Tobit of Naphtali, carried captive to Nineveh, gave alms and buried his brethren whom Sennacherib killed in his rage after fleeing Judea.

note.label: The Dividing Hatred: Cornelius the Centurion

precepts.why:
Sennacherib came against Hezekiah and mocked his God, and one angel of the Lord went forth and smote “in the camp of the Assyrians a hundred and fourscore and five thousand: and when they arose early in the morning, behold, they were all dead corpses.” One angel killed 185,000 soldiers in their sleep. Judah was saved without bow or sword, just as Hosea said. “So Sennacherib king of Assyria departed, and went and returned, and dwelt at Nineveh”, and his own sons smote him with the sword while he worshipped in the house of Nisroch his god. He went home pissed off, and Tobit shows what he did.

Tobit was “of the tribe of Nephthali”, led captive in the time of Enemessar, which is the Greek form of Shalmaneser the fifth, out of “Nephthali in Galilee above Aser.” He is northern kingdom, carried to Nineveh. “I Tobit have walked all the days of my life in the ways of truth and justice, and I did many almsdeeds to my brethren, and my nation, who came with me to Nineve, into the land of the Assyrians.”

“The most High gave me grace and favour before Enemessar, so that I was his purveyor”, overseeing the food and rations. When Enemessar died, Sennacherib his son reigned, the same Sennacherib that attacked Hezekiah and lost 185,000 men. Tobit “gave my bread to the hungry, and my clothes to the naked: and if I saw any of my nation dead, or cast about the walls of Nineve, I buried him.” Assyria was very brutal and vicious; they would take Israelites to the top of the walls and throw them off, and Tobit would bury his brothers broken in pieces on the ground.

“And if the king Sennacherib had slain any, when he was come, and fled from Judea, I buried them privily; for in his wrath he killed many.” Why did he flee from Judea? Because he lost 185,000 men. He was mad that he could not overthrow Judah, so out of anger he started killing Ephraim. When a Ninevite complained of Tobit to the king, his goods were forcibly taken away, and “there passed not five and fifty days, before two of his sons killed him”, the same death Isaiah 37:38 records.

Then Sarchedonus, Esarhaddon, reigned and appointed Achiacharus, Tobit's brother's son, over all his father's accounts, so Tobit gained standing again through his nephew. So Isaiah shows the angel saving Judah, and Tobit shows the other side of that same day: the northern kingdom in captivity in Nineveh, bearing Sennacherib's wrath, and a faithful Naphtalite burying his brethren.

moments.label: The Dividing Hatred: Cornelius the Centurion

points: Sennacherib mocked the God of Hezekiah, and one angel slew 185,000 Assyrians in the night. Judah was saved without bow or sword, as Hosea said.
Tobit of Naphtali, carried captive to Nineveh, gave alms and buried his brethren whom Sennacherib killed in his rage after fleeing Judea.

note.label: The Dividing Hatred: Cornelius the Centurion

points: When Hezekiah hears the words, he rends his clothes, covers himself with sackcloth, and goes into the house of the Most High. He turns to the Most High rather than to Egypt or to fear.

note.label: Isaiah 37: Hezekiah's Prayer and the Overthrow of the Assyrians

points: He sends Eliakim, Shebna, and the elders of the priests, covered with sackcloth, to Isaiah the prophet. He calls it a day of trouble, rebuke, and blasphemy.

note.label: Isaiah 37: Hezekiah's Prayer and the Overthrow of the Assyrians

points: He asks that Isaiah pray for the remnant that is left, hoping the Most High will hear the words of Rabshakeh, who was sent to reproach the living God. Hezekiah seeks the prophet's intercession.

note.label: Isaiah 37: Hezekiah's Prayer and the Overthrow of the Assyrians

points: This is exactly what happened: Sennacherib was killed in his own land by his own sons, showing the word of the Most High through Isaiah came to pass. No nation can stand against Israel when the Most High has spoken against it.

note.label: Isaiah 37: Hezekiah's Prayer and the Overthrow of the Assyrians

points: Isaiah answers the servants: tell your master, Be not afraid of the words with which the servants of the king of Assyria have blasphemed Me. The Most High answers the blasphemy directly.

note.label: Isaiah 37: Hezekiah's Prayer and the Overthrow of the Assyrians

points: Behold, I will send a blast upon him, and he shall hear a rumor and return to his own land, and I will cause him to fall by the sword in his own land. This is the prophecy that Sennacherib would be killed at home.

note.label: Isaiah 37: Hezekiah's Prayer and the Overthrow of the Assyrians

points: Rabshakeh returns and finds the king of Assyria warring against Libnah, for he had departed from Lachish. Word comes of Tirhakah king of Ethiopia coming out to make war.

note.label: Isaiah 37: Hezekiah's Prayer and the Overthrow of the Assyrians

points: Sennacherib sends messengers again to Hezekiah, telling him not to let the God in whom he trusts deceive him that Jerusalem will not be given into his hand. He renews the same threat and mockery.

note.label: Isaiah 37: Hezekiah's Prayer and the Overthrow of the Assyrians

points: He points to all the lands and kings that Assyria destroyed, Gozan, Haran, Rezeph, and the rest, asking whether they were delivered. He counts Jerusalem as one more city to fall.

note.label: Isaiah 37: Hezekiah's Prayer and the Overthrow of the Assyrians

points: Hezekiah receives the letter, reads it, goes up to the house of the Most High, and spreads it before Him. He lays the whole threat out before the Most High in prayer.

note.label: Isaiah 37: Hezekiah's Prayer and the Overthrow of the Assyrians

points: He calls on the Lord of hosts, God of Israel, who dwells between the cherubims, as the God alone of all the kingdoms of the earth, who made heaven and earth. He asks Him to incline His ear and hear the words of Sennacherib that reproach the living God.

note.label: Isaiah 37: Hezekiah's Prayer and the Overthrow of the Assyrians

points: He acknowledges that Assyria has laid waste the nations and cast their gods into the fire, but those were no gods, only the work of men's hands, wood and stone. He asks the Most High to save them, that all the kingdoms of the earth may know that He alone is the Lord.

note.label: Isaiah 37: Hezekiah's Prayer and the Overthrow of the Assyrians

points: Isaiah sends to Hezekiah that the Most High has heard his prayer against Sennacherib. The virgin daughter of Zion has despised and laughed him to scorn.

note.label: Isaiah 37: Hezekiah's Prayer and the Overthrow of the Assyrians

points: Sennacherib reproached and blasphemed the Holy One of Israel, boasting by his chariots that he climbed the mountains and cut down the cedars and dried up the rivers. His pride is set against the Most High Himself.

note.label: Isaiah 37: Hezekiah's Prayer and the Overthrow of the Assyrians

points: The Most High declares that He formed and brought it to pass of ancient times, that Sennacherib should lay waste the defended cities, and that the inhabitants were weak because the Most High allowed it. Because of his rage against the Most High, He will put His hook in his nose and His bridle in his lips and turn him back the way he came.

note.label: Isaiah 37: Hezekiah's Prayer and the Overthrow of the Assyrians

points: The sign to Hezekiah is that this year they eat what grows of itself, the second year what springs of the same, and the third year they sow, reap, plant vineyards, and eat the fruit. The Most High promises restoration and provision.

note.label: Isaiah 37: Hezekiah's Prayer and the Overthrow of the Assyrians

points: The remnant that escapes of the house of Judah takes root downward and bears fruit upward, for out of Jerusalem goes forth a remnant. The zeal of the Lord of hosts performs this.

note.label: Isaiah 37: Hezekiah's Prayer and the Overthrow of the Assyrians

points: Concerning the king of Assyria, the Most High says he shall not come into this city, nor shoot an arrow there, nor come before it with shields, nor cast a bank against it. Jerusalem is not going to be touched.

note.label: Isaiah 37: Hezekiah's Prayer and the Overthrow of the Assyrians

points: By the way he came, by the same he shall return, and shall not come into the city. The Most High will defend the city to save it for His own sake and for His servant David's sake.

note.label: Isaiah 37: Hezekiah's Prayer and the Overthrow of the Assyrians

points: The angel of the Most High goes forth and smites the camp of the Assyrians, a hundred and eighty-five thousand, and in the morning they are all dead corpses. One angel destroys the whole army, proving no nation stands against Israel when the Most High defends it.

note.label: Isaiah 37: Hezekiah's Prayer and the Overthrow of the Assyrians

points: Sennacherib departs and returns and dwells at Nineveh, and as he worships in the house of Nisroch his god, his sons Adrammelech and Sharezer smite him with the sword and escape into Armenia. The prophecy of Isaiah 37:7 is fulfilled: he falls by the sword in his own land, killed by his own children.
Esarhaddon his son reigns in his stead. The Most High's word stands from beginning to end.
